intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the PVRL1 gene (NECTIN1; 600644) on chromosome 11q23. Heterozygosity for a PVRL1 nonsense mutation has been associated with susceptibility to nonsyndromic orofacial cleft-7 (OFC7), which is included here.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the PVRL1 gene (NECTIN1).
checks.evidence_quote: we describe positional cloning of the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2), which we identify as PVRL1
checks.explanation: The abstract names PVRL1 as the gene for autosomal recessive CLPED1 but does not say the mutations are homozygous (abstract only).

checks.claim: The PVRL1 gene is located on chromosome 11q23.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The abstract does not give the chromosomal location 11q23.

checks.claim: Heterozygosity for a PVRL1 nonsense mutation has been associated with susceptibility to nonsyndromic orofacial cleft-7 (OFC7).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The abstract links heterozygosity for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation W185X to nonsyndromic CL/P. The OFC7 label is OMIM nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome, also called Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome or Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia, is an autosomal recessive disorder. Its main features are cleft lip and/or palate, ectodermal dysplasia affecting the hair (sparse, short, dry hair), teeth (hypodontia and dental anomalies) and nails, and partial cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers and/or toes. Some affected individuals have intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is also called Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Only the title was supplied; it does not mention the eponym 'Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome' (the name derives from the authors, but the text does not state it).

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is also called Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: These families were detected in a relatively isolated and inbred population with very small neighbouring communities from a Caribbean Sea island, Margarita Island, in Northeastern Venezuela (Nueva Esparta State).
checks.explanation: The abstract describes an ectodermal dysplasia found on Margarita Island, but it never uses the name 'Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia' or links the condition to the cleft lip/palate syndrome name.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2)
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the syndrome is autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Cleft lip and/or palate is a main feature of cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: presenting ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, syndactyly of fingers 2-3
checks.explanation: The 3 affected brothers all had cleft lip/palate.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome includes ectodermal dysplasia affecting the hair, with sparse, short, dry hair.
checks.evidence_quote: showed hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia
checks.explanation: The abstract describes sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair in a single patient. It does not mention short hair or present these hair features as general features of the syndrome.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome includes ectodermal dysplasia affecting the teeth, with hypodontia and dental anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: showed hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia
checks.explanation: The abstract reports hypodontia in one patient. It does not mention dental anomalies more broadly.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome includes ectodermal dysplasia affecting the nails.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. Only the title was supplied; it does not describe nail involvement.

checks.claim: Partial cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers and/or toes is a main feature of cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: syndactyly of fingers 2-3
checks.explanation: The abstract reports syndactyly of fingers 2-3 only. It doesn't call it partial or cutaneous, and it doesn't mention the toes.

checks.claim: Some individuals with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome have intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: presenting ectodermal dysplasia, cleft lip/palate, mental retardation, syndactyly of fingers 2-3
checks.explanation: All 3 affected brothers had mental retardation, which fits the claim that some patients have intellectual disability.

paragraphs.text: The disorder is also known as Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome, after the authors of the early case reports, and as Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia, because many cases come from Margarita Island, off the coast of Venezuela.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is known as Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome after the authors of the early case reports.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract does not use the name Zlotogora-Ogur syndrome or explain where it came from. Oğur is an author of this paper, but the naming is not stated.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is known as Margarita Island ectodermal dysplasia because many cases come from Margarita Island, off the coast of Venezuela.
checks.evidence_quote: the high frequency of CLPED1 on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a high frequency on Margarita Island (Caribbean Sea). It does not mention Venezuela or explain where the name comes from.

paragraphs.text: Zlotogora et al. (1987) described sibs with cleft lip/palate, ectodermal dysplasia involving the hair, teeth and nails, syndactyly, and intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Zlotogora et al. (1987) described sibs with cleft lip/palate.
checks.evidence_quote: Two sibs with a syndrome including cleft lip and palate
checks.explanation: The paper reports two sibs with cleft lip and palate.

checks.claim: The sibs described by Zlotogora et al. (1987) had ectodermal dysplasia involving the hair, teeth and nails.
checks.evidence_quote: sparse scalp hair, malformed protruding ears
checks.explanation: Hair involvement (sparse hair, pili torti) is reported; teeth and nails are not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: The sibs described by Zlotogora et al. (1987) had syndactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: partial syndactyly of the fingers and toes are reported
checks.explanation: Both sibs had partial syndactyly.

checks.claim: The sibs described by Zlotogora et al. (1987) had intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: The older child also has mental retardation and pili torti.
checks.explanation: Only the older sib had mental retardation, not both sibs.

paragraphs.text: A high frequency of the syndrome was recognized on Margarita Island, Venezuela, where affected individuals had cleft lip/palate together with hypotrichosis, dental anomalies, nail dysplasia and partial syndactyly. Cleft lip/palate without other features was also unusually common in the island population.

checks.claim: A high frequency of cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome was recognized on Margarita Island, Venezuela.
checks.evidence_quote: the high frequency of CLPED1 on Margarita Island in the Caribbean Sea
checks.explanation: The high frequency is stated, but the abstract places the island in the Caribbean Sea and does not name Venezuela.

checks.claim: Affected individuals on Margarita Island had cleft lip/palate together with hypotrichosis, dental anomalies, nail dysplasia and partial syndactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate
checks.explanation: The features are listed for the disorder in general, not specifically for island patients, and the syndactyly is not described as partial.

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate without other features was unusually common in the Margarita Island population.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract mentions Margarita Island only as the home of the recessive CLPED1 syndrome. It does not say that isolated cleft lip/palate was unusually common there; only the abstract was supplied.

paragraphs.text: Several families included affected sibs born to unaffected parents, some of whom were consanguineous. This pattern is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance, which was confirmed by the finding of homozygous PVRL1 mutations (Suzuki et al., 2000).

checks.claim: Several families with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome included affected sibs born to unaffected parents.
checks.explanation: The abstract gives no family or pedigree details.

checks.claim: Some parents of affected sibs with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome were consanguineous.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention consanguinity.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive inheritance of cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome was confirmed by the finding of homozygous PVRL1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: positional cloning of the gene responsible for an autosomal recessive CL/P-ectodermal dysplasia (ED) syndrome (CLPED1; previously ED4; ref. 2), which we identify as PVRL1
checks.explanation: Autosomal recessive inheritance and PVRL1 mutations are stated, but the abstract does not say the mutations are homozygous or that they confirmed the inheritance pattern.

paragraphs.text: In families from Margarita Island, Suzuki et al. (1998) mapped the disease locus to chromosome 11q23 by homozygosity mapping and linkage analysis.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (1998) studied families from Margarita Island with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Haplotype analysis of four complex Margarita Island ED4 families localized the ED4 gene to an approximately 1-2-Mb interval spanned by just two YACs.
checks.explanation: The paper studied Margarita Island ED4 families.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (1998) mapped the cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome locus to chromosome 11q23 by homozygosity mapping and linkage analysis.
checks.evidence_quote: We have used an affected-only DNA-pooling strategy to carry out linkage disequilibrium mapping of the ED4 gene to 11q23.
checks.explanation: The 11q23 mapping is correct, but the stated method was affected-only DNA-pooling linkage disequilibrium mapping with haplotype analysis, not homozygosity mapping and linkage analysis as such.

paragraphs.text: In affected individuals from Margarita Island, Suzuki et al. (2000) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the PVRL1 gene, trp185-to-ter (W185X). PVRL1 encodes nectin-1, a cell-cell adhesion molecule of adherens junctions that also serves as a receptor for herpesviruses. Suzuki et al. (2000) also found PVRL1 mutations in affected families from other populations.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (2000) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation W185X (trp185-to-ter) in the PVRL1 gene in affected individuals with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome from Margarita Island.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention the W185X mutation or its zygosity (abstract only).

checks.claim: PVRL1 encodes nectin-1, a cell-cell adhesion molecule of adherens junctions.
checks.evidence_quote: PVRL1, encoding nectin-1, an immunoglobulin (Ig)-related transmembrane cell-cell adhesion molecule that is part of the NAP cell adhesion system
checks.explanation: The abstract calls nectin-1 a cell-cell adhesion molecule but does not mention adherens junctions.

checks.claim: Nectin-1, encoded by PVRL1, serves as a receptor for herpesviruses.
checks.evidence_quote: Nectin-1 is also the principal cell surface receptor for alpha-herpesviruses (HveC; ref. 7)
checks.explanation: The abstract states that nectin-1 is a herpesvirus receptor.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (2000) found PVRL1 mutations in families with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome from populations other than Margarita Island.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention mutations in families from other populations.

paragraphs.text: Sozen et al. (2001) studied individuals with nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate in northern Venezuela. Heterozygosity for the W185X mutation was more common in patients than in controls, suggesting that heterozygous carriers have an increased risk of nonsyndromic orofacial clefting (OFC7).

checks.claim: Sozen et al. (2001) studied individuals with nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate in northern Venezuela.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The study population was people with sporadic nonsyndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.

checks.claim: Sozen et al. (2001) found heterozygosity for the PVRL1 W185X mutation more commonly in patients with nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate than in controls.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a significant association but never mentions controls or carrier frequencies. The patient-versus-control comparison is implied but not stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: Sozen et al. (2001) suggested that heterozygous carriers of the PVRL1 W185X mutation have an increased risk of nonsyndromic orofacial clefting (OFC7).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: A highly significant association between being a heterozygous carrier and CL/P directly implies that carriers are at increased risk.

paragraphs.text: Suzuki et al. (2000) found that patients with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome from Margarita Island, Venezuela, were homozygous for a trp185-to-ter (W185X) nonsense mutation in the PVRL1 gene.

checks.claim: Suzuki et al. (2000) found that patients with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome from Margarita Island, Venezuela, were homozygous for the PVRL1 nonsense mutation W185X (trp185-to-ter).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention W185X or homozygosity in Margarita Island patients (abstract only).

paragraphs.text: Sozen et al. (2001) found the heterozygous W185X mutation more often in patients with nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate from northern Venezuela than in controls.

checks.claim: Sozen et al. (2001) found the heterozygous PVRL1 W185X mutation more often in patients with nonsyndromic cleft lip/palate from northern Venezuela than in controls.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The association is stated, but the abstract does not explicitly mention controls or compare frequencies.
